public_payload.normalized_proposition: The AI industry's future depends on infinite resources, and most AI companies are front-ends for Anthropic and OpenAI models.

statement.excerpt: This industry’s future is predicated entirely on the existence of infinite resources, and most AI companies are effectively front-ends for models owned by Anthropic and OpenAI, two other companies that rely on infinite resources to run their services and fund their infrastructure.

from_speaker: models owned by Anthropic and OpenAI
our_interpretation: The checkable component is the majority claim. Most means more than half of companies by count.
Read front-ends as companies whose principal AI product depends mainly on OpenAI or Anthropic models, without assuming that their own software adds no value.
The surrounding discussion concerns generative-AI startups. Treat those as the working population, while flagging that the wording could encompass a broader AI industry.
Use January–March 2026, the latest completed operating quarter before the post, for this ongoing-state observation.
Infinite resources is rhetorical language with no finite threshold or deadline. It cannot independently receive a factual score.
criteria.support_condition: A representative company-level census or survey for the target period shows that more than half of the relevant companies principally depend on OpenAI or Anthropic models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Equivalent representative evidence shows that half or fewer principally depend on those providers.
